title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Grothendieck's manuscript on the Gauss–Manin connection, set in the relative situation S over T. Here E is an O_S-module with an integrable connection d^0_E: E → E⊗Ω^1_{S/T}, and E⊗Ω^•_{S/T} is its de Rham complex. On the previous page he gave a general description of H^1 of a complex. For a complex K^• of abelian sheaves on a topos, H^1(S,K^•) is the set of isomorphism classes of pairs (P^0, ξ), where:
- P^0 is a K^0-torsor;
- ξ is a section of P^1 = P^0 ×^{K^0} K^1;
- the image of ξ in P^2 is the canonical section, which exists because d^1d^0 = 0.

This page first reformulates ξ. A trivialization of P^1 is the same as a map of sheaves of sets d̄^0: P^0 → K^1 that is equivariant along d^0. In additive terms, d̄^0(x+f) = d̄^0(x) + d^0(f) for x ∈ P^0 and f ∈ K^0; Grothendieck writes the torsor action multiplicatively as xf. The cocycle condition on ξ then says exactly that d̄^0 takes values in Z^1K = Ker(d^1).

Specialization to de Rham cohomology. Take K^• = E⊗Ω^•_{S/T}. Then H^1_DR(S,E) classifies E-torsors P together with a map d_P: P → E⊗Ω^1_{S/T} (formula (17)) satisfying (18):
- d_P(x+f) = d_P(x) + d^0_E(f);
- d^1_E ∘ d_P = 0.
He calls this an integrable connection on the torsor P, compatible with the connection on E. Equivalently it is a crystal-type structure on an affine bundle, or an extension of (O,d) by (E,∇) in the category of modules with integrable connection.

NB, for ∇ not necessarily integrable. The compatible connections on a given torsor P are treated as first-order infinitesimal parallel transport. Grothendieck makes three claims:
- If S is affine they exist: E is quasi-coherent, so P is trivial and one can set d_P(x_0+f) = ∇f.
- Hence they exist locally.
- They form a torsor under E⊗Ω^1, isomorphic to the pushout P ×^{E,∇} (E⊗Ω^1).
So the obstruction to existence is the image of [P] under the map H^1(S,E) → H^1(S,E⊗Ω^1) induced by ∇. This is the start of the long-exact-sequence or hypercohomology interpretation, which the next page continues.
errors: Up to sign, the torsor of compatible connections is the pushout of P along -∇ (or the inverse of the ∇-pushout). The map x ↦ [x, -d_P x] gives a section of P ×^{E,-∇}(E⊗Ω^1). This is a harmless convention issue.
'homomorphisme de faisceaux d'ensembles' should be read as just a map of sheaves of sets; d_P is affine, not additive.
The second condition in (18) is consistent with the first only because d^1_E d^0_E = 0, i.e. integrability. This is implicit; the NB correctly drops it in the non-integrable case.
Existence on affine S tacitly uses that E is quasi-coherent, so that H^1(S,E) = 0 and P is trivial.

ideas.what: H^1 of a complex of abelian sheaves as classes of K^0-torsors with a trivialization of the induced K^1-torsor satisfying a cocycle condition, equivalently equivariant maps P → Z^1K
ideas.modern_name: torsor description of hypercohomology H^1 (Picard stack of a 2-term complex)
ideas.where_published: Closely related material in SGA4 Exp. XVIII (Deligne) and SGA7 VII (Grothendieck, biextensions/torsors)

ideas.what: H^1_DR(S,E) classifies E-torsors with integrable connection compatible with ∇_E
ideas.modern_name: de Rham H^1 as torsors/extensions with integrable connection (cf. universal vectorial extension E^♮)
ideas.where_published: Ideas present in Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (1968) and in the Barsotti–Tate/Dieudonné crystal program; the exact torsor formulation is unsure

ideas.what: Compatible connections on an E-torsor form a torsor under E⊗Ω^1, isomorphic to the pushout of P along ∇; obstruction to existence lies in H^1(S,E⊗Ω^1)
ideas.modern_name: Atiyah-class-type obstruction for connections on affine bundles

deep.surprise_reason: These are clean but standard foundational reformulations: hypercohomology H^1 as torsors with extra structure, and de Rham H^1 as torsors with integrable connection. The material is well known (Mazur–Messing, Deligne) and serves as routine set-up for the Gauss–Manin discussion.
transcription_corrections: 'Ceci s'explicite immédiatement à la description' is more likely 'Ceci s'applique immédiatement à la description'.
In (17) the target has a crossed-out Z followed by (E⊗Ω^1_{S/T}). The braces in the transcription are just the strike-out; the target is E⊗Ω^1_{S/T}, with Z^1 intended later in (18).
'intégrable' is inserted only once, before or after 'connexion' (the transcription duplicates it).

The NB sentence likely reads: 'Il est clair que si S est affine, il existe de telles connexions, donc il en existe très localement, et que les connexions forment un torseur sous E⊗Ω^1, qu'on voit être isomorphe à P×^E(E⊗Ω^1) (grâce à d^0_E : E→E⊗Ω^1)'.
Phrase about 'vecteurs infinitésimaux' is roughly: 'ce qui équivaut à la donnée de ... infinitésimal généralisé ... d'ordre 1'; the reading remains uncertain.
